title: How Computers That Learn From Old Storms Are Helping Forecasters
summary: When the first hurricane of this Atlantic season formed, a computer model that learns from history beat the traditional models at guessing where it would go. In early October, Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, as a Category 2 storm. Traditional models first predicted it would head farther west, toward southeastern Louisiana. But Google DeepMind's artificial intelligence model got it right from the start: the storm would hit the western Florida Panhandle. Meteorologist Michael Lowry calls DeepMind the gold standard model, and says it has been by far the best-performing computer model forecasters have ever seen. The National Hurricane Center first added the DeepMind model to its official forecasts last year, and by the end of the 2025 season it was already one of the best at predicting a storm's path and strength. Traditional physics-based models use live data on temperature, humidity, pressure and wind shear, gathered by satellites and aircraft, then use complicated equations to work out a storm's path and strength. An AI model works differently: it looks for patterns by studying thousands of past storms and atmospheric data. A neural network is a set of computer programs modeled on the human brain and trained to find patterns in huge amounts of data. That can feel like a black box, because forecasters do not always know why it is right or wrong. DeepMind's model and one from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts have proved most accurate so far. The Hurricane Center still blends several proven models, both AI and traditional, and humans interpret the results before telling the public. Brennan says forecasters turn shifting outputs into clear guidance. DeepMind topped other models on Isaias's path, Brennan says, but did not do as well as the blended forecast on the storm's strength.
why_it_matters: Better storm-path guesses give people more time to prepare, and forecasters still check several models and use human judgment before warning the public.

background_read: A hurricane is a huge rotating storm that forms over warm ocean water and can bring strong winds and heavy rain to land.
Forecasters try to guess where a storm will go and how strong it will be, so people have time to get ready.
Older models use live measurements and physics equations to work out a storm's path, while a learning model looks for patterns in many past storms.
A neural network is a set of computer programs that learns by finding patterns in very large amounts of data, though people do not always know why it picks a certain answer.
